**Summary of analysis:**

Test image features: corn leaf with one large elongated tan/cream lesion (somewhat irregular, broader than a typical thin cigar shape) and a lighter yellowish-white stripe running along the right side of the leaf lengthwise.

**Comparison:**
- **Northern_Leaf_Blight**: Best match — NLB_127 shows elongated tan/cream lesions on green leaves, very similar shape and color to the test image's main lesion. The parallel lighter stripe is consistent with a second coalescing NLB lesion.
- **Stewart's Disease**: Bleached leaf streaks are similar, but Stewart's typically shows more uniform lengthwise streaking rather than the isolated large lesion seen here.
- All others (GLS, SCLB, Goss's Wilt, Anthracnose, rusts, smuts, viral diseases) showed clearly different patterns.

The elongated tan/cream lesion with the accompanying lighter area running along the leaf is most consistent with Northern Leaf Blight.
